title: Design system — Editorial
description: Warm paper, ink and an oxblood accent, with serif headings made for reading.
forWho: Publishers, writers, journals and cultural brands

Who writes for the Review?

Essayists, critics and the occasional poet.

tiles.title: Design system — Editorial
tiles.hero:
The house style

Set for
reading.

Warm paper, ink-dark text, serif headings and one oxblood accent.

EssaysIssuesNewsletters
tiles.text:
## Principles

- Reading comes first: body text is set for long reading, never squeezed.
- Ink on paper: warm grounds, near-black text, one accent used sparingly.
- Hierarchy by type, not boxes: size and weight do the work.

## Starter profile

- **Fits:** publishing, media, journals, books, museums, nonprofits, consulting. Not for developer tools, children.
- **Mood:** warm, formal; density airy; shape sharp; contrast standard; light first.
- **Type:** Fraunces, Source Serif 4, Source Sans 3, ui-monospace.
- **Adapt first:** primary, link, ring. **Keep:** background, foreground, font-body.

## Using tokens

Use a token by its name, never its value. Change a value here and every screen and every component sample below follows: colors, type, spacing, corners, shadows, opacity and motion. Each color shows its light and dark values and is checked against the color it is read on.

## Using components

Build screens from the components in this system. Each one is drawn below in its states, with a note on when to use it. When one is missing, add a row to Components.

## Accessibility

Text reaches 4.5:1 against what it sits on; control edges and focus 3:1. Focus is always visible. Nothing is told by color alone.
